title: The Monkey as King
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: At a gathering of all the animals the Monkey danced and delighted them so much that they made him their King. The Fox, however, was very much disgusted at the promotion of the Monkey: so having one day found a trap with a piece of meat in it, he took the Monkey there and said to him, "Here is a dainty morsel I have found, sire; I did not take it myself, because I thought it ought to be reserved for you, our King. Will you be pleased to accept it?"

The Monkey made at once for the meat and got caught in the trap. Then he bitterly reproached the Fox for leading him into danger; but the Fox only laughed and said, "O Monkey, you call yourself King of the Beasts and haven't more sense than to be taken in like that!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why is the Monkey made King of the animals?
options: He won a contest of strength
He was the oldest animal present
He danced and delighted them all
He offered the best gift at the gathering

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox feel about the Monkey's promotion?
options: Very much disgusted
Genuinely pleased
Completely indifferent
Secretly hopeful for his own turn

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox find one day?
options: A cave filled with treasure
A lost crown belonging to another king
A group of hunters setting up camp
A trap with a piece of meat in it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say about why he didn't take the meat himself?
options: He was too full to eat any more
He thought it ought to be reserved for the King
He was afraid of getting caught in the trap
He wanted to share it with the other animals first

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens when the Monkey goes for the meat?
options: He successfully eats the meat and escapes
He shares the meat with the Fox
He gets caught in the trap
He realizes it is a trap and refuses it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Monkey do once he is caught?
options: He bitterly reproaches the Fox for leading him into danger
He laughs along with the Fox
He orders the Fox to free him at once
He blames himself for being careless

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox say about the Monkey calling himself "King of the Beasts"?
options: That the title suits him perfectly well
That the other animals will soon regret their choice
That he deserves the title more than any other animal
That he hasn't more sense than to be taken in like that

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox offer the meat to the Monkey instead of simply setting the trap for him another way?
options: The Fox wants to prove his loyalty to the new King
Flattering the Monkey as King makes him more likely to walk straight into the trap
The Fox is afraid to touch the trap himself
The Fox genuinely wants to reward the Monkey for his dancing

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what point is the Fox making about the qualities that make a good ruler?
options: Foxes make better kings than monkeys in every situation
Traps are the best way to test a ruler's wisdom
Being entertaining does not necessarily mean having the good judgment a ruler needs
Kings should never accept gifts from their subjects

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Charm and talent alone do not guarantee the wisdom needed to lead well
Foxes are always jealous of any animal chosen as King
Traps are impossible to detect no matter how careful one is
Animals should never elect a leader based on a single talent

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox call the meat when he speaks to the Monkey?
options: A rare treasure
A tasty reward
A royal feast
A dainty morsel

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox address the Monkey when offering the meat?
options: "Friend"
"Sire"
"Your Majesty"
"Old fellow"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox react to the Monkey's complaints after he is trapped?
options: He apologizes sincerely
He rushes to free the Monkey
He only laughs
He calls for the other animals to help

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Fox present the meat as something reserved specially for the King?
options: It appeals to the Monkey's pride, making the trap harder for him to resist
It is simply a factual description of how the Fox found the trap
It is meant to warn the Monkey away from danger
It is meant to test whether the Monkey trusts the Fox

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Fox's laughter suggest about his true feelings toward the Monkey's new title?
options: He feels genuine sympathy for the Monkey's misfortune
He is embarrassed that his trick worked so easily
He regrets tricking an animal he actually admired
He never respected the Monkey's rule and is satisfied to see him humbled

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "reproached" mean in "he bitterly reproached the Fox"?
options: Thanked warmly
Blamed or criticized
Questioned calmly
Ignored completely

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Fox helps the Monkey become a wiser King
The Monkey outsmarts the Fox's trick and avoids the trap
A jealous Fox tricks the newly crowned Monkey King into a trap using flattery
The other animals punish the Fox for disrespecting the King
